newsitem.title: USA: MSRB actions mixed on pol parties, consultants.
newsitem.headline: MSRB actions mixed on pol parties, consultants.

text.p: The Municipal Securities Rulemaking Board voted not to tighten regulation of the contributions that bond dealers make to political parties, panel chairman Roger Hayes announced Tuesday.

But the 15-member board, which met three days last week, did vote to propose expanding information that bond dealers must disclose quarterly about the political consultants they hire to lobby municipal issuers, Hayes added.
"We admit we think we may see some smoke out there," Hayes told reporters concerning questionable dealer contributions to political parties.
"But we have to figure out if it is a campfire or forestfire before we write a rule affecting every (dealer firm) in this country," Hayes continued.
Therefore, the board voted to make information about dealer contributions to political parties more widely available by publishing it over the MSRB's Internet website, Hayes said.
But it opted not to amend its pay-to-play rule G-37 by adding party contributions to the list of dealer activities that can trigger a ban under the April 1994 rule, Hayes said at a press briefing.
Rule G-37 bars broker dealers who contribute to issuer clients from doing negotiated bond business with those localities for two years afterward.
Hayes said the information to be published on Internet will be broader than just party contributions. He said all data reported to the board on forms G-37 and G-38 will be made available on the Net.

Regarding disclosure of consultants' contributions, the board's rule G-38 currently requires muni dealers to disclose information quarterly to the board about their arrangements with consultants they use to help them win bond business.
Hayes said the board will propose a rule requiring more contribution-specific data.
"Right now rule G-38 says you have to have a contract with the consultant that states the basis of the compensation," Christopher Taylor, executive director of MSRB, said.
"That provision will be modified to say that you also must furnish the dealer with information regarding any contributions," he said.
